findings.title: CodeQL #112: claimed path injection in document-failure test callback

normalized_input.claimed_sink: path.write_bytes in nested test callback write_partial_then_fail
normalized_input.claimed_control: Claimed missing path constraint across atomic_generate callback dispatch
normalized_input.affected_version_or_path: Reported main ecd987dcaecce05eed13391a765f27cf5b9def76; inspected local 3e9ed3b6ea4263ee0958574f79ac12829a5b14d5 with identical affected/call-path blobs
preconditions: The API request would need to dispatch the nested regression-test callback as the production writer.
normalized_input.impact: Claimed unexpected filesystem write through a request-influenced path
references: CodeQL Python SARIF analysis2100597990; ref refs/heads/main; reported commit ecd987dcaecce05eed13391a765f27cf5b9def76

affected_locations.label: reported source
affected_locations.detail: The API calls materialize_reviewed_preview; it does not accept or select a writer callback from the request.

affected_locations.label: actual production writers
affected_locations.detail: Actual atomic_generate calls pass document.save or fixed local text/PDF/manifest lambdas.

affected_locations.label: callback dispatch
affected_locations.detail: Calls the writer argument supplied by that invocation on its temporary path.

affected_locations.label: reported sink
affected_locations.detail: Nested test-only callback is created inside one unittest method; that invocation uses TemporaryDirectory and a fixed resume.pdf destination.

reachable_path: The imported SARIF offers four paths from the cover-letter API through production atomic_generate calls to the test callback.
Concrete Python call sites pass other writer objects on those four production paths.
The test callback exists only inside its unittest method and is passed by that test to _generate_document_artifact with a fixture-owned destination.
No supported request-to-test-callback dispatch path is present in the inspected code.

boundary_assessment.policy_basis: Root SECURITY.md identifies synthetic least-privilege CI and forbids treating successful scans as security certification. No scoped SECURITY.md exists for the inspected ancestors. The actual closure/call sites, rather than a test-directory label or packaging assumption, establish this specific boundary.

exploitability_stack_rank.rationale: Concrete callback identity defeats the reported API-to-test-sink path.

evidence: Read the alert instance and all four code-flow paths from main Python SARIF analysis2100597990.
Inspected the API entrypoint, all four cited production writer call sites, atomic_generate, _generate_document_artifact, and the complete test.
Target and call-path blobs were verified identical between reported main and the unchanged local checkout; the worktree remained clean.
Scoped callsite search in apps/services/workers/cli/tests found the nested callback only at its definition and local test invocation.
counterevidence: Production calls do not pass write_partial_then_fail; the nested closure is not an exported request-selected callback.
The actual test invocation supplies a TemporaryDirectory-derived destination and fixed filename.
Bundling tests in an image does not itself make this local closure reachable through the API; no exclusion-by-filename assumption was used.
proof_gaps: Static assessment only: no tests, PoCs or runtime validation were executed for this triage.
Other production path-injection alerts, including reviewed-cover-letter aliasing addressed by open PRs, are outside this verdict.
The skill's shared policy-resolver/reference resources were unavailable; applicable root/ancestor policy files were enumerated and read manually.
findings.recommended_next_step: Record the narrow static non-actionable rationale for alert112. Keep alert state unchanged unless an authorized maintainer separately reviews dismissal; continue triage of the production sinks independently.

findings.title: CodeQL #57: incomplete URL prefix assertion in mocked discovery test

normalized_input.claimed_source: URL strings collected in the synthetic test's seen list
normalized_input.claimed_sink: str.startswith check against a fixed synthetic employer origin
normalized_input.claimed_control: The unparsed URL comparison does not require exact hostname equality
normalized_input.affected_version_or_path: Reported main ecd987dcaecce05eed13391a765f27cf5b9def76; identical test blob a605c4f39a8a335b063c3c9919a1c294f7317d73 at inspected local 3e9ed3b6ea4263ee0958574f79ac12829a5b14d5
preconditions: Treating the post-execution unittest assertion as a production URL authorization decision.
normalized_input.impact: Potentially weak test assertion; scanner suggests URL-check bypass
references: CodeQL Python SARIF analysis2100597990; ref refs/heads/main; reported commit ecd987dcaecce05eed13391a765f27cf5b9def76

affected_locations.label: fixture setup
affected_locations.detail: The test creates a temporary SQLite workspace and fixed synthetic company/profile inputs.

affected_locations.label: synthetic response path
affected_locations.detail: The method records a fixed verified domain and patches _request_once with a local response function backed by a static pages dictionary.

affected_locations.label: reported control
affected_locations.detail: The prefix expression is only a final unittest assertion; it does not authorize a request, redirect, or subsequent filesystem operation.

reachable_path: A unittest method creates a fixed synthetic company/domain and static page responses.
Its local patched request function appends URLs to seen and returns an in-memory HTTP response.
After execute_operation returns, the method asserts completion and checks those observations with startswith.
No runtime behavior consumes the assertion result as an authorization or routing decision.

boundary_assessment.policy_basis: Root SECURITY.md specifies synthetic CI and preserved privacy boundaries. No nearer scoped policy exists. The patched request implementation and post-execution assertion establish the actual surface; this is not a claim that every test file or production URL policy is safe.

exploitability_stack_rank.rationale: The flagged expression is an observation assertion, not a supported security-boundary control.

evidence: Read the main alert instance and matching SARIF result, which has no code-flow chain.
Inspected the complete method, fixture setup and the static response implementation.
The test blob is identical between reported main and local revision; the checkout remained clean.
counterevidence: The lower network boundary is replaced by a local synthetic response function during this method.
The prefix check is evaluated after the operation and solely feeds assertTrue.
The scanner identifies a real weakness in exact-host test precision, but the supplied location does not enforce production egress.
proof_gaps: Static review only; no tests, PoCs, live employer requests or runtime validation were executed.
Production URL admission and other SSRF alerts were not exhaustively reviewed.
The unavailable shared policy helper was replaced with explicit root/ancestor policy-file inspection.
findings.recommended_next_step: Record the narrow non-actionable security verdict. Consider exact parsed scheme/hostname comparison as ordinary test-strength maintenance; do not infer production SSRF safety or dismiss other alerts.
